text_blocks.snippet: To manage COVID-19 symptoms, focus on relieving discomfort and preventing further spread. Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help with fever and pain. Rest and hydration are crucial, and isolating from others can help protect them from infection. If symptoms worsen or cause concern, seek advice from a healthcare provider.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on relieving discomfort and preventing further spread

list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications: Use acetaminophen (e.g., Tylenol) or ibuprofen (e.g., Advil, Motrin) to manage fever, aches, and pains, according to the CDC.
Rest: Get plenty of rest to allow your body to recover.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids, like water, broth, or electrolyte drinks, to stay hydrated.
Isolation: Stay home and separate from others in your household, especially if you have worsening symptoms, according to the Mayo Clinic.
Face Mask: Wear a face mask if you must be around others, says the Mayo Clinic.
Hygiene: Practice good hygiene, like frequent handwashing, covering coughs and sneezes, and cleaning and disinfecting surfaces.
Separate Items: Avoid sharing personal items like towels, cups, and utensils.
Ventilation: Improve airflow in your living space.

list.title: Worsening symptoms:
list.snippet: If your symptoms are getting worse or causing you significant concern, consult with a healthcare provider, according to the Canadian government.

list.title: Specific symptoms:
list.snippet: Pay attention to symptoms like difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain or pressure, confusion, or bluish lips or face. Seek immediate medical attention for these symptoms.

list.title: General advice:
list.snippet: If you have any questions or concerns about your symptoms, consult with your healthcare provider, advises the CDC.
